finding.description: The small jar initially contains only green olives, but as they are poured into the large jar, several black/dark purple olives fall out, changing color mid-air.
The second small jar also appears to contain only green olives before being poured, but black olives fall from it into the large jar.
The person pours from a jar containing only green olives, but a mixture of green and dark purple/black olives falls out and lands in the larger jar. The effect does not match the cause.
The person pours from a second jar containing only green olives. As the olives fall, a mix of green and dark olives comes out of the jar and lands in the larger container.
A watch with a light blue band suddenly appears on the person's left wrist as they reach towards the bowls on the right, whereas the wrist was clearly bare earlier in the same continuous shot.
The stream of falling olives renders over the top of the large jar's front rim, clipping directly through the solid glass barrier rather than falling behind it into the opening.
As the olives settle at the bottom of the large jar, they fail to behave as solid rigid bodies, visibly clipping into and merging with one another in the pile.
During the second pour, the falling stream of olives again clips through the front glass rim of the large jar instead of passing cleanly through the opening.
The olives in the small jar are uniformly green. As they are poured and fall through the air into the large jar, many of them instantly transform into black/dark purple olives.
Across a cut, the volume of olives in the large jar abruptly decreases. The jar goes from being approximately half full at 00:03 to noticeably less full at 00:05, with no visible action of removal.
During the second pour, the olives inside the small jar are again exclusively green, but transform into a mix of green and black olives as they fall into the large jar.

As the olives are poured, the stream of falling olives is rendered in front of the near-side rim of the large receiving jar. Since they are falling into the jar's opening, they should be occluded by the front rim.

During the second pour, the bottom edge of the small pouring jar and the falling olives are again rendered overlapping the front rim of the large jar, violating the expected depth ordering for objects entering the opening.
